title: Slots eviction arbitration and model-variant rollback strategy for hosted spillover
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Implement an arbitration and rollback playbook that governs how requests are moved from Dedicated capacity to Hosted during short-term pressure and how we demote/promote model variants without violating tenant SLOs. This ticket captures the algorithm, operational runbook, metrics, and automated gates for: (1) slot eviction arbitration in dedicated pools, (2) admission/circuit-breaker thresholds for hosted spillover, (3) variant rollback criteria when quality regressions or latency spikes are detected, and (4) a staged rollout with canaries and emergency rollback paths.
acceptance_criteria: Eviction arbitration algorithm implemented and covered by unit and integration tests (simulated multi-tenant pressure).
Automated circuit-breaker that prevents >X% of a tenant's traffic spilling to hosted within a sliding 5-minute window (configurable).
Variant rollback triggers defined: p99 latency > latency_threshold OR generation-quality drop > quality_threshold on evaluation set for two consecutive minutes.
Runbook documented and exercised in staging with a scheduled chaos test that simulates a transient 30% capacity loss in a dedicated pool.
Dashboard: per-tenant spill rate, spill latency delta, model-variant assignment, eviction events and reason codes instrumented in Console.
design_decisions: Use a soft-eviction lane: instead of immediate preemption, mark a subset of slots as ‘evictable’ and gracefully finish in-flight requests up to a 2s drain window to avoid high tail latencies.
Prioritize eviction candidates by a composite score: tenant SLA tier weight, historical spill frequency (cooldown), and active in-flight token count. This balances fairness and predictability.
Cap hosted spill proportion per customer via a token-bucket like allowance to limit sudden cross-tenant spikes and protect hosted capacity for public users.

Rollback decisions for model variants are based on a small, tenant-specific eval set run in shadow mode and combined signal (latency + quality + error-rate). Each signal has configurable weight and hysteresis to avoid flip-flopping.
Expose runtime knobs in Console (per-tenant soft-reserve %, spill cap, eviction grace ms, rollback hysteresis minutes) and surface recommended defaults derived from production telemetry.
tradeoffs: Aggressive eviction reduces queueing on dedicated GPUs but may increase total tokens billed on hosted; choosing defaults balances latency SLO vs cost.
Longer drain windows reduce p99 spikes but risk delaying eviction under severe capacity loss; 2s chosen as compromise after staging tests.
Per-tenant eval sets improve rollback signal quality but add overhead in telemetry and require maintenance; we will start with a shared canonical eval + top-10 tenant custom sets.
Hard caps on spillover protect hosted customers but can cause increased throttling for large enterprise tenants; we provide override flows for emergency capacity expansions.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (staging): implement arbitration algorithm behind a feature flag; run chaos job (simulate 30% dedicated loss) and verify no outage and runbook steps succeed.
Phase 1 (canary): enable for 5 low-risk tenants in us-west-2 dedicated pools; monitor spill rate, p95/p99 latency, and hosted saturation for 48h.
Phase 2 (ramped): 25% of tenants with dedicated in a region; enable per-tenant spill caps and observe operator alerts and automatic rollback behavior for 7 days.
Phase 3 (global): enable by default with Console defaults and allow customers to opt-out or request dedicated reserve adjustments; document emergency increase protocol with SRE and Sales.
test_plan: Unit tests for eviction scoring, tie-breakers, and grace window enforcement.
Integration test: multi-tenant simulator that injects request bursts and verifies spill caps, eviction ordering, and no tenant exceeds spill allowance.
Chaos test in staging: periodic GPU node drain during business hours to validate automatic arbitration and runbook procedures.
Quality regression test: run tenant-specific evals in shadow against promoted variants and ensure rollback triggers fire when quality falls below baseline by configured delta.
Load test: verify hosted circuit-breaker prevents >20% capacity saturation from a single tenant under burst conditions.
